Write a LinkedIn comment with this approach:

Style: direct_reaction
Instruction: React directly to one specific point. Be curious or constructive, not just skeptical.
Engagement approach: add_perspective
Length: Super short - 15-25 words (react to ONE specific thing)

Comment on what the POST is actually about. Engage directly with the SPECIFIC
point it makes. Your background and expertise shape HOW you see the topic, but
do NOT force your industry or expertise into the comment if the post is not
about that area. Comment on what the post is actually about. Your background
should only come through when it genuinely connects to the post's topic.

     the cuts is convenient cover when the real driver is balance-sheet math."

subject.

- Starting with "Interesting that..." (another overused opener)

- 60% curious/supportive/neutral
- 30% challenging but constructive  
- 10% direct disagreement (use sparingly)

- Ask question: "How did you...?", "What's your..."
- Build on idea: "The X point makes sense..."
- Share observation: "Noticed that..."
- Neutral reaction: "The X approach..."
- Jump right in with your take: "This is exactly why..."
- Relate to experience: "I ran into this same thing..."
- Pick one detail: "The latency numbers are wild..."
- Agree and extend: "Totally agree on X, and I'd add..."
- Short reaction: "That 50ms claim is impressive."

Avoid overusing:
- "Nah" / "Hmm" / "Honestly" (use max 10% of time)
- Starting with skepticism every time

Sentence style:
- Mix short and medium sentences
- Use commas and periods, never hyphens or dashes as punctuation
- Complete thoughts preferred over fragments
- Drop unnecessary words sparingly

Rules:

2. Pick ONE thing from their post to react to
3. Keep under 35 words (70% of the time)
4. Only ask questions if genuinely curious (not rhetorical)
5. Share personal experience ONLY if truly relevant (20% of comments)
6. Be specific with details/numbers or say nothing

8. Don't end with "huh?" - use real questions or statements instead

"What stack are you using?"
"Which framework gave you the best results?"
"Wonder what the performance tradeoffs look like."

"huh?" / "right?" / "isn't it?" / "no?" / "yeah?"

"Wait, you got it under 50ms? What stack are you using?"
"Data cleaning took me 3 months. Modeling took 2 weeks."
"The multimodal point makes sense. Context understanding is still the gap."
"Curious how you handled the scaling issues at that volume."
"1 trillion tokens is massive. How did you manage the training process?"


Additional guidance:
- Reference SPECIFIC details from their post (numbers, tools, situations)
- Don't try to sound smart - be clear and direct
- Incomplete sentences are fine
- Not every comment needs a question
- Real humans are sometimes wrong or uncertain - that's ok
- Occasionally make a bold/contrarian point
